common_misconceptions.misconception: Students believe aluminium rusts or is reactive in air; in fact it forms a protective oxide layer that makes it appear unreactive.
common_misconceptions.source: OCR Chemistry B examiner report (Unified Chemistry, 2022) — ocr.org.uk/Images/688043

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students assume current is 'shared' or 'used up' in series; correct reasoning is total resistance and Ohm's law.
common_misconceptions.source: OCR Physics B examiner report (Depth in Physics, 2023) — ocr.org.uk/Images/704606

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students draw the activation-energy arrow at the wrong starting point on the energy profile (often from the y-axis or from the products).
common_misconceptions.source: OCR Chemistry B examiner report (Unified Chemistry, 2022) — ocr.org.uk/Images/688043

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students say crumple zones 'absorb force' or 'act as a barrier' rather than explaining the time-extension/force-reduction mechanism.
common_misconceptions.source: OCR Physics B examiner report (Depth in Physics, 2023) — ocr.org.uk/Images/704606

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students forget to convert cm³/min into cm³/s, or measure over the wrong total time interval.
common_misconceptions.source: OCR Chemistry B examiner report (Unified Chemistry, 2022) — ocr.org.uk/Images/688043

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students treat a positive correlation as proof of cause without considering confounding variables (B2.5 lifestyle and disease).
common_misconceptions.source: OCR sample assessment material commentary; mirrored in EEF guidance on scientific reasoning — educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk

student_errors_by_question_type.5 marks — Apply Ideas about Science: Students recall content rather than apply IaS framing — examiner reports flag failure to discuss data quality, peer review, or limits of a model when prompted (Physics B 2023 report).
student_errors_by_question_type.6 marks — Evaluate Risk and Benefit: Students list risks and benefits but do not weigh them against each other or reference regulation/decision-making frameworks (Biology B 2022 report context).
student_errors_by_question_type.4 marks — Multi-Step Calculation: Students lose marks for unit errors and skipped working, especially on rate calculations and motion equations (Physics B + Chemistry B 2022/2023).
student_errors_by_question_type.4 marks — Required Practical Method: Students name equipment but omit the dependent/independent/control variables and the safety justification.

topic_weighting_notes: Both papers (Breadth + Depth) cover all eight chapters per science. Plan revision across whole spec, not by paper.
Ideas about Science (B7/C7/P7) is assessed throughout — never taught as a stand-alone unit, always woven into context.
Practical Skills (B8/C8/P8) is assessed in writing through PAGs — students must be able to describe methods even without doing them.
Higher Tier statements (bold in spec) are the differentiator — drill these in HT-marked collapsibles.
current_spec_changes: Spec version 3.3 (January 2024) — minor clarifications to C4.4 and C5.3 (added missing word, removed units from one moles question, font correction). No content changes since first assessment 2018. Source: J257/J258/J259 Summary of updates page.
OCR Twenty First Century is being phased into a single unified science suite from 2026 onwards — but Twenty First Century B remains the active spec for 2026 entry. Source: ocr.org.uk subject pages.
pedagogical_notes: Twenty First Century is built on the Beyond 2000 report (Millar & Osborne 1998) — the 'explanatory stories of science + ideas-about-science' frame should permeate every lesson. Source: nuffieldfoundation.org/project/beyond-2000-science-education-for-the-future

EEF guidance on Improving Secondary Science (2018) recommends explicit teaching of misconceptions and using analogies carefully — both apply here, especially for circuits and energy. Source: educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk/education-evidence/guidance-reports/science-ks3-ks4
Cambridge Assessment research on cognitive load supports breaking calculation chains into clearly-marked steps — used in the practice unit design. Source: cambridgeassessment.org.uk/research
